title: Home
description: tzsp-monitor landing page, served as Grafana's default home (GF_DASHBOARDS_DEFAULT_HOME_DASHBOARD_PATH). Edit grafana/entrypoint/home.json, not this dashboard; when adding a dashboard, list it here too.

options.content: Network traffic, intrusion detection and DNS filtering from one mirror. Pick a dashboard below, or use Dashboards in the menu: the folders follow the same order.

### 1 · Overview
*Start here: is anything wrong, and where is the traffic going?*

**[Network Health](d/network-health)**  
Wallboard. Traffic vs yesterday, active hosts, fan-out, every tile with a status word.

**[Network Monitor](d/tzsp-network-monitor)**  
Top applications (nDPI), top talkers with hostnames, throughput and packet rate.

**[Network Topology](d/network-topology)**  
Who talks to whom: the busiest links as a node graph.

**[Sites Overview](d/sites-overview)**  
Every configured site summed on one screen.

### 2 · Traffic Analysis
*From the whole network down to a single host.*

**[Application Categories](d/app-category-overview)**  
Bytes by nDPI category and application, and who drives each.

**[Services & Ports](d/services-ports)**  
Traffic by service and port, cleartext protocols, TLS/DNS server names.

**[Upload vs Download](d/traffic-direction)**  
Direction split per host and service, and uploads to public addresses.

**[Traffic Baseline](d/traffic-baseline)**  
What normal looks like: hour-of-week heatmap and flow-size profile.

**[Zone Traffic Matrix](d/zone-traffic-matrix)**  
Zone-to-zone traffic, egress and ingress per zone.

**[Subnet Top Talkers](d/subnet-top-talkers)**  
Bytes per segment and the top hosts inside one.

**[Subnet Hosts](d/subnet-hosts)**  
Every host in a subnet you type: traffic, reverse-DNS name, MAC and NIC vendor.

**[Host Drill-Down](d/host-drilldown)**  
One IP: its peers, applications, latest flow records, and its MAC and vendor.

### 3 · Security
*Detections first, then behaviour that no signature covers.*

**[Suricata Alerts & Auto-Block](d/suricata-alerts)**  
IDS alerts by severity, router blocks, pipeline and disk health, rule tuning.

**[Anomaly Watch](d/anomaly-watch)**  
Fan-out, beacon candidates, new talker pairs and new destinations.

**[Port Scanners](d/port-scanners)**  
Who is scanning: attempts that fan out and never complete, ping sweeps, ET SCAN alerts; the ports each one tried.

**[Ethernet Attacks](d/ethernet-attacks)**  
ARP spoofing and poisoning, IP conflicts, ARP sweeps; who answers for every IP, with its NIC vendor.

**[TCP Health](d/tcp-health)**  
SYN/RST/FIN rates, reset ratio and connection completion.

**[IP Reputation Blocking](d/ip-reputation)**  
Control surface: public blocklists (Spamhaus DROP, Feodo C2, ...) onto a router address list.

**[Packet Capture](d/packet-capture)**  
Control surface: record the mirror to pcap files, by network, and list them.

**[Wireless IDS](d/wireless-ids)**  
The air rather than the wire: evil twins, spoofed APs, deauth floods, KARMA, handshake harvesting; every AP heard.

**[Alerting](d/alerting)**  
Control surface: run a shell command (a webhook via curl) when any detector finds something, per source and severity.

### 4 · DNS
*Who looked up what, and the filter that refuses names.*

**[DNS Activity](d/dns-activity)**  
Lookups per client, and every blocked name with the host that asked.

**[DNS Web Filter](d/dns-web-filter)**  
Control surface: choose the UT1 categories the router blocks.
